methodologyNotes: Covers portable outdoor cooking stoves sold at a published US MSRP, spanning canister backpacking stoves, integrated cooking systems, liquid/multi-fuel expedition stoves, biomass (wood) stoves, and tabletop/car-camping burner stoves. Excludes fixed home ranges, built-in RV cooktops, and bulk-propane grills without a stove burner. Price is US MSRP (typical retail) in USD. fuelType is an enum: one of 'isobutane-propane-canister', 'butane-cartridge', 'propane-cylinder', 'white-gas-multifuel', or 'wood-biomass'. burnerCount is the number of independent cooking burners (integer). outputBtuHr is the manufacturer-rated maximum total heat output summed across all burners, in BTU per hour. boilTimeSecPerLiter is the manufacturer-stated time to bring 1 liter of water to a boil, in seconds; null if not disclosed. ignitionType is an enum: 'piezo' (integrated push-button igniter), 'manual' (requires external match/lighter), or 'battery-spark'. simmerControl is a boolean: true if the stove has an adjustable valve capable of a low simmer flame. integratedPot is a boolean: true if the stove is sold as a system with a locking/dedicated cooking vessel included. windscreenIntegrated is a boolean: true if a built-in or attached windscreen/wind-blocking burner is part of the stove as sold. weightGrams is the manufacturer-published packed weight of the stove as sold (including the pot for integrated systems), in grams. packedDimensionsIn is the folded/stowed footprint as 'L x W x H' in inches.

products.name: SOTO WindMaster
products.priceNote: US MSRP $69.95 from the official SOTO USA store page (sotooutdoors.com), which lists the "WindMaster Stove with 4Flex" (OD-1RXN) at "$ 69.95". The Amazon listing displayed EUR 61.27 due to geo-locale, so it was not used for the USD figure.
products.provenance: The SOTO USA manufacturer store page identifies this exact model as the WindMaster with 4Flex, product #OD-1RXN (which replaced the older OD-1RXC; the stove itself is unchanged), and lists it at "$ 69.95", confirming both the US MSRP and model identity. That page states Output "2800 kcal/h 3260w 11000 BTU", a Micro Regulator valve, a Stealth (piezo) igniter, a built-in windscreen (concave burner head), and weight "3.0 oz (87g) with the 4Flex pot support". The Amazon SOTO Store listing corroborates the same OD-1RXN part number, 11000 BTU output, isobutane fuel, "Item Weight 87 Grams", built-in windscreen, and piezo ignition (its displayed price appeared in EUR due to geolocation, so the USD MSRP was taken from the manufacturer page); boilTimeSecPerLiter and packedDimensionsIn were left null because neither page discloses a per-liter boil time or a single combined stowed footprint for the product as sold.

products.name: Jetboil Flash
products.priceNote: US MSRP $129.99, sourced verbatim from The Trek's Jetboil Flash 1.0L Fast Boil System review (2025-06-26): "MSRP: $129.99" (repeated as "$129.99" in the cons section). Treeline Review (2025-09-17) independently lists the price as "$130".
products.provenance: Jetboil's official page (jetboil.johnsonoutdoors.com/.../flash-10l-fast-boil-system) is behind an Incapsula WAF and returns no machine-readable content, so I anchored on two independent dated reviews of the exact model — the 2025-redesigned "Jetboil Flash 1.0L Fast Boil System" with the new turn-and-click ignition (confirmed by name and feature set as this model, not the MiniMo, Stash, or older Flash). The Trek (source, 2025-06-26) reproduces the manufacturer at-a-glance sheet verbatim: "MSRP: $129.99", "Weight: 13.088 oz | 371 g", "Power: 5300 BTU/h / 1.5 kW", "Dimensions (Packed): 4.25 in x 7.5 in", isobutane-propane JetPower fuel, and turn-and-click ignition. Treeline Review (corroboration, 2025-09-17) independently confirms the $130 price, the "Turn-and-click piezo igniter", no simmer capability ("SIMMER? No"), and the integrated 1 L FluxRing pot ("INTEGRATED POT? Yes"), matching model identity; boilTimeSecPerLiter is null because only the 0.5 L boil time (120 sec) is disclosed, not a 1-liter figure.

products.name: MSR PocketRocket 2
products.priceNote: US street price $50 per Switchback Travel review (Last Updated October 10, 2024): stated verbatim as "Price: $50", again as "$50" in the comparison table, and "Affordably priced at $50". The official MSR/Cascade Designs product page displays no US price (EU-locale store shows an empty EUR cart only).
products.provenance: The official MSR (Cascade Designs) product page for the PocketRocket 2 Stove, SKU 09884, confirms the exact model and its Tech Specs verbatim: Minimum Weight 73 g / Packaged Weight 105 g, Dimensions 1.3 x 1.6 x 3.1 in, boil time 3.5 minutes for 1 liter on MSR IsoPro, torch-to-simmer flame control, and a built-in WindClip windshield; the page lists no BTU rating and no igniter. The Switchback Travel review (Last Updated October 10, 2024) corroborates this same PocketRocket 2 (explicitly distinct from the $85 PocketRocket Deluxe), stating "Price: $50", "Fuel Type: Canister", "Auto Ignition: No", "Pot: No", and a claimed 3.5-minute 1L boil time. Price is taken verbatim from that dated review ($50) since the manufacturer page shows no US price; outputBtuHr is left null because MSR does not publish a BTU rating and the review's "8,200" is a reviewer comparison figure, not a manufacturer rating.

products.name: MSR WhisperLite International
products.priceNote: US retail price sourced verbatim as "$159.95" from Tooth of Time Traders (Philmont Scout Ranch store, store.philmontscoutranch.org), listed for the "MSR WHISPERLITE INTERNATIONAL STOVE". The official MSR/Cascade Designs product page did not display a USD price (EU storefront returned EUR), so price is taken from the US retailer.
products.provenance: The official MSR/Cascade Designs product page (SKU 14044) confirms this is the WhisperLite International multi-fuel stove and states its tech specs verbatim: packaged weight 14.9 oz (423 g), folded dimensions 6 x 4 x 4 in, white-gas 1-liter boil time of 3.5 minutes (recorded as 210 s), and fuel compatibility of white gas, kerosene, and unleaded auto fuel; its includes list (fuel pump, windscreen, heat reflector, small-parts kit, stuff sack) shows a separate foil windscreen and no integrated igniter, and its FAQ states only the DragonFly among MSR liquid-fuel stoves has a fully adjustable simmer flame (hence simmerControl false). The official page showed no USD price (EU storefront), so price is sourced from US retailer Tooth of Time Traders (Philmont Scout Ranch), which lists the identical model at $159.95 with the same fuel compatibility and boil times, confirming model identity. The retailer separately lists the plain "WisperLite" at $139.95, disambiguating this entry as the multi-fuel International variant rather than the white-gas-only base model.

products.name: Camp Chef Everest 2X
products.priceNote: Camp Chef official product page (campchef.com/products/everest-2x) lists the Everest 2X, SKU MSHPX, at "Regular price $229.99" — used as US MSRP. Amazon corroborates the same model (Model/Part Number MSHPX) but shows only localized EUR pricing; the Switchback Travel review lists a $190 street price. Cited figure is the manufacturer's $229.99.
products.provenance: The Camp Chef official product page (campchef.com/products/everest-2x) confirms the exact model "Everest 2X", SKU MSHPX, at a "Regular price $229.99", with two 20,000 BTU burners, 215 sq. in. of cook space, matchless ignition, and a folding lid that forms a 3-sided windscreen. The Amazon listing (corroboration) matches Model/Part Number MSHPX for the "Camp Chef Everest 2X 2-Burner" and states 40,000 total BTUs (dual 20K burners) with Propane / Liquefied Petroleum Gas fuel and the folding-lid windscreen, confirming this is the exact model, not a sibling. A Switchback Travel hands-on review of the same model additionally confirms a piezo (matchless) igniter and excellent simmer control. Weight and packed dimensions were left null because the only figures found conflict (Amazon 15 lb / 27x15.5x8.25 in vs. review 12 lb) and no manufacturer-published packed figure was available verbatim in grams.

products.name: Coleman Cascade Classic 2-Burner Camp Stove
products.priceNote: Authorized Coleman retailer Sports Basement lists the Cascade Classic at "$ 99.99". Independent dated reviews corroborate typical retail near this: Better Trail (Apr 15 2025) cites $100 and CleverHiker (Feb 14 2025) lists $98. Coleman's own MSRP page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; $99.99 used as typical US retail.
products.provenance: source.url is Coleman's official product page for the exact "Cascade Classic" 2-burner model, but it returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so specs were verified verbatim against authorized Coleman retailer Sports Basement (corroboration.url), which reproduces Coleman's full spec sheet: 20,000 total BTUs across two propane (16 oz cylinder) burners, 21 x 12.8 x 3.6 in stowed dimensions, Instastart rotary ignition, two integrated wind guards, precise simmer control, and a $99.99 price. Model identity is confirmed as the Cascade Classic (not the Cascade 222, the 3-in-1, or the older match-lit Classic): a dated hands-on review (Better Trail, Apr 15 2025) independently corroborates the same model with two 10,000-BTU burners (20,000 total), propane fuel, rotary piezo auto-ignition, and built-in wind shields at ~$100. A second dated review (CleverHiker, Feb 14 2025) confirms the 20,000 BTU / 10,000-per-burner propane figures, though it describes no auto-ignition, apparently conflating the older match-lit Classic; the manufacturer spec sheet and Better Trail both confirm the Cascade Classic ships with integrated rotary/piezo ignition.

The Amazon.com listing (Primus Express Stove, Model/Part 1442480, GTIN 07330033321401) shows "Currently unavailable" with no US price (the EUR figures on the page are for unrelated suggested products). The 68travel product page (Primus article P321484) lists no price. The only officially priced Express SKU is the separate piezo variant P321485 at $54.99 on primus.us, which is a different model and was not used. priceUsd left null.
products.provenance: 68travel's product page for Primus article P321484 — the base, non-piezo Express Stove — reproduces the manufacturer spec table (Material Stainless Steel/Brass; Power 2600 W; Fuel Consumption 185 g/h; Diameter 131 mm; Height 87 mm; Weight g 83) and lists "Control valve for precise flame control" with no piezo igniter, confirming an adjustable-valve, manual-ignition, single-burner canister-top stove sold with only a nylon bag (no pot, no windscreen). The Amazon.com listing (Primus Express Stove, Model/Part 1442480, GTIN 07330033321401) corroborates the same model — Fuel Type Isobutane, EN417 screw cartridge, Maximum Energy Output 2600 Watts — and states the Express ships "with or without" the optional "Easy-Trigger" piezo, identifying this base SKU as the manual version, distinct from the piezo variant P321485 sold on primus.us. No US MSRP appears on either fetched page (Amazon shows "Currently unavailable"; 68travel lists no price), so priceUsd is null; outputBtuHr, boilTimeSecPerLiter and packedDimensionsIn are null because the pages give only "2600 W" (no BTU/hr), a words-only/conflicting boil time ("2.30 min" vs "three and a half minutes"), and packed dimensions in mm (no inch figure).

products.name: BioLite CampStove 2+
products.priceNote: US MSRP $199.95, from BioLite official product page ('Regular price $199.95') for the base CampStove 2+. The Better Trail review listed inconsistent figures ($200 and $250, the $250 referring to the Complete Cook Kit bundle SKU), so the manufacturer figure was used.
products.provenance: The BioLite official product page (bioliteenergy.com/products/campstove-2-plus) confirms this exact model — "CampStove 2+" — at a Regular price of $199.95, with Tech Specs listing Fuel "Biomass (sticks, twigs, pellets)", Boil Time "4.5 minutes for 1L" (= 270 s), Weight "2.06 lbs (935g)", and packed Dimensions "5.0" x 7.91""; the FAQ ("light with a match or lighter") and the In-The-Box list (no pot; KettlePot sold separately) establish manual ignition and no integrated pot. The dated Better Trail review (Apr 14, 2025) corroborates the CampStove 2+ identity and specs — Fuel Type Biomass, "Auto Ignition: No", "doesn't come with any wind shields" (no integrated windscreen), and no usable temperature control (no simmer valve). outputBtuHr was left null because BioLite publishes no BTU rating and the review's 10,000-BTU figure is internally inconsistent (stated both as the total max and as "10,000 BTUs each" on this single-chamber stove); the review's "2" burner count is a template artifact contradicting its own prose, so burnerCount was recorded as 1 for this single-combustion-chamber stove.
